_meta.purpose: Classification of every trapLine in pro-repertoires.json into one of three kinds. Drives whether a trapLine surfaces as a bright-red TRAP tile in the line picker (only kind:'trap'), or stays internal as a punish-stage lesson with a softer label (kind:'mistake') or middlegame theme (kind:'theme'). Without this file the picker treated every trapLine as a real trap and the user reported the bright-red flood — many entries are mislabeled by the curator (gambit-accepted positions, slight structural advantages, long maneuvering lines). User: 'How would you organize this mess of data I have now vomited through the app?'

kinds.trap: Opponent's natural-looking move has a CONCRETE tactical refutation forcing material gain or mate within ~3 plies. Examples: Noah's Ark Trap, Legal's Mate, Nb5-Nc7 fork, Stafford Queen trap, Qb6-Nb5 queen trap. Surfaces as a red TRAP tile.
kinds.mistake: Opponent blunders, you punish via principle (counting, structural, tempo) — no forced tactical refutation, just 'now you're better.' Examples: doubled pawns from a6 Bxc6, gambit accepted with structural edge, knight chases that lose tempo. Stays internal as punish-stage lesson.
kinds.theme: Long maneuvering line about middlegame plans, structural ideas, fortress, bishop pair, pawn storms — not a punishment for an opponent's move at all. Examples: Berlin Wall bishop pair, KID kingside storm, Stonewall fortress, Catalan diagonal pressure. Stays internal.
